story.title: The Exit Name
story.logline: A woman discovers that every time she forgets someone's name, they physically vanish from the world.
story.theme: The weight of human memory and existence.
story.twist: She realizes the reason she is forgetting everyone is because she is the next one to vanish, forgotten by the last person left.
story.ending: If you don't remember my name right now, will I even exist tomorrow?

scenes.narration: My best friend never existed. I watched her completely erase from reality just because I forgot her middle name.
scenes.visual_prompt: Vertical 9:16 video. Maya, a 25-year-old woman with shoulder-length dark hair wearing an oversized green hoodie, stands alone in a brightly lit modern apartment looking terrified at an empty chair.
scenes.camera: Close-up on Maya's panicked face, push in slowly.

scenes.narration: It sounds insane, right? But the universe has a cruel rule. If a name fades from your mind, the body goes too.
scenes.visual_prompt: Maya, 25, dark hair, green hoodie, paces anxiously across the same modern apartment, clutching her head with both hands.
scenes.camera: Medium tracking shot following her movement.

scenes.narration: Last week, it was my neighbor Leo. I called him Luke in my head for one second. Poof. Gone.
scenes.visual_prompt: Maya, 25, dark hair, green hoodie, points a shaking finger at an empty doorway inside the same apartment.
scenes.camera: Over-the-shoulder shot looking into the empty hallway.

scenes.narration: Now I write every single name on my arms, my walls, my phone. I guard them like stolen gold.
scenes.visual_prompt: Maya, 25, dark hair, green hoodie, frantically scribbling names in black marker all over her bare arms inside the brightly lit apartment.
scenes.camera: Extreme close-up on her arms and the marker ink.

scenes.narration: My little brother Ben is next. I can feel the memory slipping like sand through my sweaty fingers.
scenes.visual_prompt: Maya, 25, dark hair, green hoodie, staring at a framed photograph of a boy on a wooden table, her hands trembling.
scenes.camera: Focus pull from the photo to Maya's blurred face.

scenes.narration: His face is blurring. His laugh is turning into static. I scream his name over and over to anchor him.
scenes.visual_prompt: Maya, 25, dark hair, green hoodie, shouting silently with tears streaming down her face in the center of the apartment.
scenes.camera: Low angle rotating slowly around her.

scenes.narration: And then, my brother blinks out of existence right in front of me. The photo frame is completely empty.
scenes.visual_prompt: Maya, 25, dark hair, green hoodie, staring down at the wooden table where the photo has turned into blank photo paper.
scenes.camera: Top-down bird's-eye view of the empty frame.

scenes.narration: I am completely alone now. No family, no friends left. Just me and the quiet, empty apartment.
scenes.visual_prompt: Maya, 25, dark hair, green hoodie, standing motionless in the middle of the vast, silent room.
scenes.camera: Wide static shot emphasizing her smallness.

scenes.narration: Except, I look down at my own reflection in the dark window glass, and my own name is vanishing from my lips.
scenes.visual_prompt: Maya, 25, dark hair, green hoodie, touching the glass of a dark window, her fingers beginning to turn semi-transparent.
scenes.camera: Close-up on her reflection dissolving at the edges.

scenes.narration: If you don't remember my name right now, will I even exist tomorrow?
scenes.visual_prompt: Maya, 25, dark hair, green hoodie, looking directly into the camera lens as her entire body fades into white light.
scenes.camera: Extreme close-up staring straight into the camera.

caption.hook: Forgetting names makes people vanish entirely.
caption.title: The Exit Name
caption.caption:
What if forgetting someone wasn't just a lapse in memory, but an absolute erasure from reality? The scariest part isn't losing them—it's realizing why you can't remember anyone at all.

Who are you terrified of forgetting?
